neighbours.label: the end of a clause that limits or qualifies a claim, where a contrast ('but', 'however') is expected next ('extremely subjective', 'to the contrary', 'hard to generalize from it;'), as opposed to plain unqualified statements
fire: The sample was tiny, so we should not read too much into it; more work is needed.
Judging art is highly subjective and critics rarely agree.
There is no strong evidence to the contrary, so the claim stands for now.
The rules were generally followed; however, a few exceptions occurred.
It would be nice to own a boat, but that is not realistic for us.
Minor colds can usually be treated at home. However, see a doctor if fever persists.
Short sentences are effective to that end. But longer ones have their place.
The results are promising, though it is too early to draw conclusions.
quiet: The sample was large, and we analysed it carefully over two years.
Judging the art contest took the critics most of the afternoon.

The rules were printed on a sheet and handed to every player.
We own a boat and take it out on the lake every summer.
Minor colds usually last about a week.
Short sentences were written on the board by the teacher.
The results were posted on the website at noon.
